correctness.rationale: Split each exponential sum at k=0: for z=exp(2πiω), r=exp(-λ), the two geometric terms are exp(-λx)/(1-r/z) and z exp(-λ(1-x))/(1-rz). Combining them gives the displayed positive denominators and numerators. At z=1 the sum is strictly positive (there may be a single zero summand at c=1 on the seam). At z=-1, cancellation factors as (v-w) times a factor depending on v+w=2√q cosh(x-1/2), giving the central zero and the spatial branch exactly between c_A and c_B, with the seam and center merger endpoints. For nonreal z, real and imaginary cancellation requires proportional numerator coefficients; off the seam this reduces to (v-w)(1-q)=0, hence x=1/2, while on the seam there is only the real equation. The resulting seam and center ratios are strictly increasing in cos(2πω), by D_2-qD_1=(1-q)(1-q³); their values at -1 are c_A and c_C and at +1 are both above 1. These cases exhaust the half-open cell, giving 1,2,5,3,5. The threshold ordering follows from c_A>1/2, c_B/c_A=(1+q)/(2√q)>1 and c_C/c_B=2c_A>1; c_C<1 follows, for example, from 1/3<q<2/5 and √q>4/7. Independent bounded sampling checked the split closed form against the raw series (maximum discrepancy 8.88e-16) and the predicted roots at all three transition values and at c=0,1; the count rests on the exhaustive analytic split.
residual_risks: The title's 'positive' is nonnegative at c=1; line 54's 'strictly positive term by term' has the noted exception, which does not affect strict positivity of the sum.

value.rationale: This gives an explicit nonnegative decaying family in which simply giving up unimodality permits two different mechanisms that create extra zeros and an interval that loses them again. The full-cell count and exact seam, spatial and frequency branch endpoints make this a useful benchmark beyond positive-unimodal or totally positive uniqueness. Positivity alone does not explain the one-zero phenomenon.
residual_risks: Does not imply quantitative frame bounds, a complete lattice-scale frame set, or a classification of all mixtures.
